primitives.name: Measure Extension Theorem
primitives.verbatim_quote: If μ is a o-finite measure on a ring R, then there is a unique measure μ on the σ-ring S(R) such that, for E in R, μ(E) = μ(E); the measure μ is σ-finite.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'μ': 'measure on ring R', 'S(R)': 'σ-ring generated by ring R', 'E': 'set in R'}
primitives.assumptions: μ is o-finite on ring R
primitives.breakdown_regime: When μ is not o-finite, extension may fail

layer2.telemetry: Consistency of measure values across R and S(R)

primitives.name: Uniqueness of Measure Extension
primitives.verbatim_quote: To prove uniqueness, suppose that μ and μ2 are two measures on S(R) such that μ1(E) = μ2(E) whenever E ε R, and let M be the class of all sets E in S(R) for which μ(E) = μ2(E).
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'μ1, μ2': 'measures on σ-ring S(R)', 'M': 'class of sets where μ1(E) = μ2(E)'}
primitives.breakdown_regime: Failure occurs if agreement fails on generating ring

layer2.mapping: Ensures GSE's deterministic evolution paths remain invariant under equivalent measure assignments.
layer2.telemetry: Monotone class property of M implies equality on S(R)

primitives.name: Sigma-Finiteness Condition
primitives.verbatim_quote: If μ is a o-finite measure on a ring R, then there is a unique measure μ on the σ-ring S(R) such that, for E in R, μ(E) = μ(E); the measure μ is σ-finite.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'σ-finite': 'measure can be expressed as countable union of finite sets'}
primitives.assumptions: μ must be o-finite on R
primitives.breakdown_regime: Non-σ-finite measures may not admit unique extensions

layer2.telemetry: Countable decomposition of measurable space into finite subsets

The σ-finiteness condition guarantees that the extended measure retains key properties necessary for probabilistic interpretation.
